question: Which government scheme aims to phase out unfit and polluting vehicles from India's roads to reduce emissions and boost automotive industry recycling?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Voluntary Vehicle Fleet Modernisation Programme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Voluntary Vehicle Fleet Modernisation Programme (V-VMP), also known as the **Vehicle Scrappage Policy**, was introduced by the Government of India in **2021**.
 
• The policy aims to phase out **unfit, old, and polluting vehicles** to reduce environmental pollution and improve road safety.
 
• It mandates fitness tests for commercial vehicles older than **15 years** and private vehicles older than **20 years**.
 
• Unfit vehicles that fail the fitness test or are not re-registered will be scrapped, promoting the recycling of automotive materials.
 
• The initiative is expected to **boost demand in the automotive industry** by encouraging the purchase of new, fuel-efficient, and cleaner vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fitness Tests:**

 
 
• Mandatory automated fitness tests are conducted at **Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities (RVSFs)**.
 
• These tests ensure vehicles meet minimum environmental and safety standards.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of the Policy:**
 
 
• Reduction in air pollution caused by older, high-emission vehicles.
 
• Promotion of recycling industries, creating economic and environmental benefits.
 
• Fuel savings through the use of modern, fuel-efficient vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Incentives for Vehicle Owners:**
 
 
• Owners of scrapped vehicles are offered incentives like **tax concessions** and discounts on the purchase of new vehicles.
 
• Scrappage certificates issued to vehicle owners can be redeemed for benefits while buying new vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Automotive Industry:**
 
 
• The policy is expected to increase demand for new vehicles, leading to growth in the automotive sector.
 
• It supports the Make in India initiative by encouraging domestic manufacturing.
